LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines three source items:

1. A release tarball from `https://github.com/Voxelum/x-minecraft-launcher/releases/download/v${pkgver}/app-${pkgver}-linux.asar.gz` – a standard upstream binary bundle.  
2. An icon file from the project's master branch `https://github.com/Voxelum/x-minecraft-launcher/raw/refs/heads/master/xmcl-electron-app/icons/dark.icns` – a static asset.  
3. A local desktop entry `xmcl.desktop` that is part of the AUR repository.

All source items have explicit SHA‑256 checksums, and none are marked `SKIP`. The PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments, function definitions, and safe command substitutions (e.g., `${pkgver}` in URLs). No top‑level code, command substitutions, or `pkgver()` logic downloads or executes arbitrary payloads. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions – which could perform file transformations, installations, or script generation – are not invoked with `--noprepare`/`--nobuild`. Therefore, fetching and extracting these sources via `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and generating srcinfo with `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe and does not execute any potentially malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Source fetches are from trusted upstream URLs; no malicious code execution.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is for the xmcl-electron-bin package, an open-source Minecraft launcher. The analysis reveals standard AUR packaging practices with no evidence of malicious or dangerous behavior.

The package downloads prebuilt binaries from the legitimate upstream GitHub repository (github.com/Voxelum/x-minecraft-launcher/releases), which is the expected source for a `-bin` package. The downloaded ASAR archive (an Electron app bundle format) is extracted using the `asar` tool (declared as a makedepends) into the package directory. The package then installs the application's icon, a `.desktop` file, and creates a standard launcher script that executes `electron42` with the app directory. None of these operations are suspicious or deviate from normal packaging.

The `sha256sums_x86_64` and `sha256sums_aarch64` are set to `SKIP`, which is a hygiene concern but is explicitly noted as standard practice per packaging guidelines and is not evidence of malice. There are no obfuscated commands, no use of `eval`/`base64`/`curl`/`wget` in unexpected contexts, no network requests to unrelated hosts, no data exfiltration, no backdoors, and no system file tampering. The launcher script is created via a simple heredoc and merely runs the electron binary with the app path, which is the conventional method for packaging Electron applications on Arch Linux.

No genuinely malicious behavior was identified. The file is consistent with ordinary packaging workflows for an Electron-based application.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>

Standard AUR packaging for electron Minecraft launcher; no malicious code found.
